First, let $u=x+1.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\text{d}x.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{x+1}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+1|+C\end{aligned}
$$

First, let $u=-\frac{11}{7}x+5.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-\frac{11}{7}\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\frac{7}{11}\text{d}u.
$$

We can now rewrite the integral in terms of $u,$ solve it, and write the final answer in terms of $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\frac{5}{6}}{-\frac{11}{7}x+5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{6}\int \frac{1}{-\frac{11}{7}x+5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{6}\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot (-\frac{7}{11}\,\text{d}u) \\  & =-\frac{35}{66}\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\frac{35}{66}\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-\frac{35}{66}\operatorname{ln}⁡|-\frac{11}{7}x+5|+C\end{aligned}
$$
